What I built: Form trigger that collects name, email, company, job role and "what are you looking for", writing each submission to a Google Sheet
What went wrong: The n8n AI assistant switched to replying in Spanish partway through the build
How I fixed it: Told it explicitly to reply in English. Lesson: check assistant output language and settings early

What went wrong: The Sheets node showed an error because it had no account or target sheet
How I fixed it: Created a "Leads" sheet with headers matching the form fields, connected my Google account, and selected the sheet

What I built: Information Extractor node using an OpenAI model to return structured JSON: segment, intent and a 1-10 score
What went wrong: Every test reused the same pinned sample lead, so I couldn't see how the AI handled different types of lead
How I fixed it: Unpinned the sample and created my own mock data with four deliberately different leads: a student, an enterprise buyer, a small business and a spam entry

What went wrong: Only 1 of the 4 test leads was saved because my JSON had a syntax error (missing braces)
How I fixed it: Fixed the JSON and confirmed the node showed "4 items" before running

What went wrong: Running from inside the trigger node only tested the trigger, so nothing reached the AI or the sheet
How I fixed it: Closed the node panel and ran "Execute workflow" from the main canvas. All four leads were classified and written to the sheet

What I built: Reviewed AI output against expected results
What went wrong: Scores were accurate (enterprise buyer 10, spam 1), but the AI labelled both the spam entry and a student as "SMB" because the schema forced a choice with no fallback. Spam would have received nurture emails
How I fixed it: Added "Unknown" segment and "Invalid" intent options, and routed invalid leads to a separate "Rejected" tab (in progress)

What went wrong: gpt-5-mini doesn't support temperature, so I added an explicit scoring rubric instead.
How I fixed it: Ran the same four leads twice after the change: scores were identical across both runs (previously varied by 1 point), and spam was rejected every time.

What I built: Hot-lead email alert via Gmail for leads that are "Ready to buy" or score 9+, on the valid-lead branch only
What went wrong: The default email included an n8n attribution footer, which wouldn't be appropriate for a client
How I fixed it: Turned off the attribution setting. Tested with four leads: only the enterprise buyer triggered an alert

What I built: Weekly leads report emailed every Monday
What went wrong: The report showed 3 rejected leads when the sheet had 1. The second sheet-read node ran once per item from the first read, tripling its results. The total and average also included spam, which skewed lead quality
How I fixed it: Set the node to execute once and separated valid and rejected counts. Averages now use valid leads only. Verified every figure by hand against the sheet
